title: I. The Goal
text:
You are B.J. Habibie, the 3rd President of Indonesia. You have 23 turns (June to October 1999) before the 700 delegates of the MPR vote on your Pidato Pertanggungjawaban (Accountability Speech) on October 19, 1999.

• Win: at least 351 votes accept your speech and you keep the presidency.
• Lose: fewer than 351 votes.
• The vote is a secret ballot. Delegates can defect.
• Metrics and factions are shown as descriptive tiers and stances, not numbers. Only Political Capital is a number.

title: II. Every Turn
text:
Each turn has two parts.

1. Crisis Event: a historical event. Pick one response. Every option changes your metrics and factions.

2. Action Phase: you may do both of these once per turn.
• One Executive Action:
  – Routine Action: costs nothing, earns Political Capital, has a cooldown, and pays less each time you repeat it.
  – Extraordinary Decree: costs Political Capital, has requirements, and its effects are permanent.
• One Faction Engagement: negotiate with a faction. It costs Political Capital, and repeating the same deal with the same faction pays less. You can engage with a faction more than once, however, each interaction after the first one costs you 5 extra Political Capital

Press CONCLUDE AGENDA to end the turn.

title: III. The Metrics
text:
Seven metrics are on the left panel. Political Capital (PC) is your spending money (maximum 100).

• Popularity: public mood. High warms delegates every turn. Low erodes their trust.
• Military Support: standing with Cilangkap. Tied to the ABRI bloc.
• Reformasi Credibility: trust of students, the press and reformers. If it collapses, the streets erupt.
• Economic Health: the rupiah and food prices. Freefall hurts Popularity and National Stability.
• International Standing: credibility with foreign capitals and the IMF. Low standing causes capital flight.
• National Stability: civic order. When it drops, every decree and negotiation costs more Political Capital.
• Cendana Influence: the power of Suharto's inner circle. High is harmful: it drains Political Capital every turn, erodes Reformasi Credibility and sabotages wavering delegates in the final vote.

Together they set your Government Stability (SECURE, STABLE, PRECARIOUS, UNSTABLE, COLLAPSING). STABLE or better gives free Political Capital each turn. UNSTABLE or worse drains it.

title: IV. The Factions
text:
Each faction cares about specific metrics. Keeping those high gives you Bargaining Leverage: negotiations cost less and win more goodwill.

• PDI-P (153 seats): Popularity, Reformasi Credibility.
• Golkar (Slipi) (80): Economic Health, National Stability, Cendana Influence.
• Golkar (Loyalists) (40): Reformasi Credibility, Economic Health, International Standing.
• PAN (34): Reformasi Credibility, Popularity.
• PKB (51): Popularity, Reformasi Credibility.
• PPP (58): National Stability, Popularity.
• Other Parties (46): National Stability, Popularity.
• ABRI (38): Military Support, National Stability.
• Utusan Daerah (135): Economic Health, National Stability.
• Utusan Golongan (65): Reformasi Credibility, International Standing.

Late in the game PAN, PKB and PPP unite as the Central Axis (163 seats).

Favors: some big concessions make a faction owe you a Favor. Cash it in with a Final Appeal in the last three turns for a large loyalty surge, or keep it for election night to steady wavering delegates. Each faction can hold only a few Favors, depending on difficulty.

title: V. Meters to Watch
text:
Two factions react to how you treat them. Check the bars on their screens.

• Military patience and anger (ABRI screen): ignore the generals and their patience drains into anger. Anger cuts what every other faction gives you and your Political Capital income. Meeting the generals holds patience. ABRI loyalty above 55 slowly drains anger.
• Street Mobilization (PDI-P screen): rises every turn you do not deal with PDI-P, and faster when they are hostile. At 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% it cuts your Political Capital, Popularity and Reformasi Credibility gains and makes PDI-P costlier to talk to. At 100% they vote to reject to the last delegate.
• Cendana Influence: cutting it too fast in one turn can trigger bank runs and street sabotage. Lower it steadily.

title: VI. Election Night and Tips
text:
How delegates vote on October 19:
• Disciplined blocs (PDI-P, ABRI) follow their leadership.
• Fragmented caucuses (Golkar (Slipi), Utusan Daerah, Utusan Golongan, Other Parties) split by their goodwill toward you, your Government Stability and Cendana Influence interference.
• Once the session starts, decrees that change seats, ban caucuses or rewrite election rules are closed.

Tips:
• Never let Political Capital sit idle. Spend it on factions that matter.
• Watch the leverage line on each faction before you pay.
• Turn on Outcome Forecast Tooltips in Settings to preview effects. They are disabled on Historical.
• Historical is the recommended difficulty. Beat it to unlock Severe State Situations.
• Your campaign is saved automatically. Use Continue Game to resume.
